teaching_notes.why_this_case_matters: KEEP example: the instruction forms one coherent local route objective (Move forward past the white coach and then turn left. Continue up the stairs and stop.). The apparent action clauses do not establish a separate completed target with a useful, source-supported handoff.
teaching_notes.reusable_rule: Keep the instruction as one stage when its turns, traversal and target selection form one coupled maneuver and no independent intermediate completion point is stated. Preserve all action order and conditions in the same stage.
teaching_notes.five_element_focus: Check entry, target, complete ordered process, supported ending, and scoped conditions in the actual English text. Audit fields cannot replace missing words.
teaching_notes.handoff_focus: A boundary is not a physical stop. Verify the previous exit and next entry refer to the same established region/object/frame.
teaching_notes.retrieval_rule: Retrieve for short or tightly coupled routes where splitting at a turn, pass-by cue or descriptive observation would create an orientation-only stage without an independent navigation target.
teaching_notes.anti_pattern: Do not split at every turn or movement verb. If the turn itself completes a distinct source-supported objective and a later independent target benefits from local focus, reassess the boundary.
teaching_notes.decision_reason: The turn changes orientation for the same continuous route leg; no independently completed intermediate objective is established before the following movement.
teaching_notes.transfer_rule: Keep preparatory turns with the movement they enable when the source supplies no separate completed target or useful handoff. Count objectives and supported outcomes, not verbs.
